title: Add queue delay + batch formation metrics for tiered batching profiles
creator: Sofia Ivanova
description:
Goal
Add runtime instrumentation to make tiered batching behavior observable and debuggable in production:
- Queue delay (time waiting to be admitted / batched)
- Batch formation stats (effective batch sizes, formation latency)
- Per-stage latency breakdown (admission -> queue -> prefill -> decode)

Why
We’re rolling out workload-aware batching defaults (fast/standard/cost-efficient). SRE and Runtime need metrics to:
- Validate p50/p95/p99 adherence per tier
- Catch tail-latency regressions driven by queueing
- Debug streaming cadence regressions (TTFT + decode cadence)
- Tune tier defaults and model/GPU overrides using real batch formation stats

Scope
1) Metrics emitted from runtime scheduler path and per-request spans.
2) Metric names + label schema that is stable for dashboards/alerts.
3) Guardrails to avoid metric cardinality explosions.

Non-goals
- Building dashboards (tracked in ENG-18427)
- Full automated tuning (post-beta)

References
- Project PRD: confluence/product-docs/requirements/workload-aware-batching-defaults-prd
- Design: confluence/product-docs/design-specs/workload-aware-batching-defaults-design-spec
- SLO tiers: confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/latency-slo-tiers-fast-standard-costefficient

Proposed metric set (v1)

A) Queue delay / admission
- redwood_inference_queue_delay_ms (HISTOGRAM)
  Definition: time from request arrival at runtime to admission into an execution batch.
  Notes: includes “waiting for batch formation” time; excludes network overhead outside runtime.

- redwood_inference_admission_result_total (COUNTER)
  Definition: total admissions outcomes.
  Values emitted via label admission_result={"admitted","shed","rejected","canceled","timeout"}.

- redwood_inference_overload_shed_total (COUNTER)
  Definition: total shed events (subset of admission_result_total) with a stable reason.
  Label shed_reason={"queue_full","kv_pressure","oom_guard","latency_guard","rate_limit","unknown"}.

B) Batch formation stats
- redwood_batch_formed_total (COUNTER)
  Definition: number of compute batches formed by the scheduler.

- redwood_batch_size (HISTOGRAM)
  Definition: number of requests in the formed batch.

- redwood_batch_wait_ms (HISTOGRAM)
  Definition: time from first eligible request enqueued for a batch to the batch being dispatched.
  Notes: used to validate tier max_queue_delay behavior.

- redwood_batch_tokens_prefill_total (HISTOGRAM)
  Definition: total prefill tokens across the batch at dispatch time (sum across requests).
  Notes: enables debugging cases where batch size is “large” but token volume still small/large.

C) Per-stage latency
- redwood_request_stage_latency_ms (HISTOGRAM)
  Definition: per-request time spent in each stage.
  Label stage={"admission","queue","prefill","decode","postprocess"}

- redwood_request_ttft_ms (HISTOGRAM)
  Definition: time-to-first-token for streaming requests (or time-to-first-byte equivalent for non-streaming).
  Notes: for non-streaming, ttft approximates “time-to-first-chunk”; keep for comparability.

- redwood_stream_token_cadence_ms (HISTOGRAM)
  Definition: inter-token time (ms) observed by the server for streaming responses.
  Notes: sampled (see guardrails) to limit overhead.

Required labels (apply consistently across the above where applicable)
(Keep label set small/stable; anything high-cardinality goes into traces only.)
- deployment_mode={"hosted","dedicated","private"}
- region=<cloud region slug, e.g. "us-east-1">
- model_family=<stable identifier, e.g. "llama3.1","qwen2.5"> (NO full model version)
- gpu_sku=<stable identifier, e.g. "a100-80g","h100-80g","l40s">
- route={"chat.completions","completions","embeddings","rerank"}
- streaming={"true","false"}
- batching_tier={"fast","standard","cost_efficient","explicit"}
- prompt_len_bucket={"0-256","257-1k","1k-4k","4k-16k","16k+"}
- concurrency_bucket={"1","2-4","5-8","9-16","17+"}

Traces (OTel span attributes)
Add span attributes for per-request debugging without impacting metrics cardinality:
- rw.effective.max_batch
- rw.effective.max_queue_delay_ms
- rw.effective.prefill_weight / rw.effective.decode_weight
- rw.queue_depth_at_arrival
- rw.kv_cache_pressure (bucketed)
- rw.batch_id (ONLY in traces)
- rw.batch_size_at_dispatch

Cardinality + overhead guardrails
- Do NOT label with: customer_id, project_id, request_id, model_version, endpoint path, prompt hash.
- Bucket prompt length + concurrency into a small finite set (see buckets above).
- Token cadence metric should be sampled (e.g., 1% of streaming requests) and documented.
- Histograms: keep a consistent bucket configuration (see implementation notes). Avoid adding too many histograms in hot paths.

Implementation notes
- Metrics emitted from scheduler hooks added in ENG-18421 / scheduler refactor.
- Prefer monotonic counters + histograms exported via our metrics pipeline.
- Ensure metrics are present in:
  - Hosted: production /metrics scrape + OTel exporter
  - Dedicated/Private: same names via runtime container
- Unit/integration test: verify metrics registry contains the series and labels (smoke test) + ensure no per-request label leakage.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Metrics above implemented in runtime behind the tiered batching feature flag (but metrics always safe to emit; tier label can be "explicit" or "unknown" when disabled).
- [x] Dashboards can compute p95 queue delay per tier/model/region and correlate with p95 end-to-end latency.
- [x] Traces include effective-config attributes and queue depth at arrival.
- [x] Cardinality reviewed with SRE (Sean/Rafael) and Observability (Allison/Logan).
- [x] Performance overhead measured in perf canary: <1% throughput impact and no measurable p95 regression in baseline.

Rollout
- Land metrics first; dashboards/alerts follow (ENG-18427).
- Once dashboards validated, use these metrics as gating signals in staged rollout (PR: canary/auto-rollback hooks).

Links
- GitHub PR (runtime metrics): sources/github/redwood/pr_18449
- Perf canary extension: sources/github/perf-canary/pr_622 (consumes these metrics)
- Observability pack dashboards: sources/github/observability-pack/pr_289 (uses these metric names)
